question: Your CloudFormation stack creates an S3 bucket. You manually added an additional bucket policy via AWS Console after stack creation. Three months later, you run a stack update. The manual policy is deleted. What happened?
options: CloudFormation drift detection failed; manual changes should have been detected
CloudFormation replaced the stack; previous configuration was lost
Stack update synced the template state; manual changes outside template are not preserved
Manual policy deletion is a bug; report to AWS support
explanation: CloudFormation is declarative; the template is the source of truth; manual changes are considered drift; updates sync to template state, overwriting manual changes; use --no-execute-rollback to detect drift.

question: Your CloudFormation template creates 50 AWS resources (EC2, RDS, Lambda, VPC, etc.). Stack creation takes 25 minutes. You need to deploy frequently (3x daily). Should you split the template into nested stacks?
options: Yes; nested stacks allow parallel creation of independent resources; reduces total time
No; nested stacks add complexity; keep monolithic for simplicity
Yes; but nested stacks slow down creation due to serialization
No; use CloudFormation change sets instead; they're faster than nested stacks
explanation: Nested stacks can deploy independent resources in parallel; splitting into dev/data/compute stacks enables concurrent creation; reduces 25 minutes to 10-12 minutes.

question: Your CloudFormation template defines an RDS database with DeletionPolicy: Snapshot. You delete the stack to clean up a dev environment. A backup snapshot is created automatically. Six months later, you're charged for an orphaned snapshot ($20/month). How can you prevent this?
options: Use DeletionPolicy: Delete to remove snapshots on stack deletion
Use DeletionPolicy: Retain; manually verify and delete snapshots
Snapshots can't be deleted via CloudFormation; this is a known AWS limitation
Schedule an S3 lifecycle rule to delete orphaned snapshots
explanation: DeletionPolicy: Snapshot preserves backups after stack deletion (good for production); DeletionPolicy: Delete removes snapshots (good for dev); choose based on environment and retention needs.

question: You have three CloudFormation templates: VPC stack (created first), app stack (depends on VPC), and monitoring stack (independent). Stack creation order is: VPC -> app -> monitoring. You want to create all three simultaneously. How?
options: Use stack dependencies; CloudFormation parallelizes based on dependencies
Export VPC outputs; app and monitoring import these exports; can be created in any order
Use nested stacks; wrap all three in a parent stack
Rewrite as a monolithic template; simultaneous creation isn't possible with multiple stacks
explanation: Exports create dependencies visible to other stacks; stacks can be created in any order if they import required exports; CloudFormation creates templates without explicit dependency; nested stacks still serialize based on parent.

question: Your CloudFormation template uses hardcoded resource names: BucketName: my-app-bucket-prod. You want to deploy the same template to dev, staging, and prod environments with different bucket names. What's the best approach?
options: Create three separate templates (dev, staging, prod); hardcode names in each
Use CloudFormation Parameters with default values; pass environment name at creation time
Use mappings to map environment to resource names; reference in template
Store names in Systems Manager Parameter Store; reference in template
explanation: Parameters allow user input at stack creation; reuse the same template across environments; mappings are static (requires template change); Parameter Store adds external dependency.

question: Your CloudFormation template has a Condition that creates a NAT Gateway only in production (condition: isProd: True). During a stack update, you change the condition from True to False to save costs. What happens to the NAT Gateway?
options: NAT Gateway is retained; conditions don't affect existing resources
NAT Gateway is deleted; CloudFormation removes resources when conditions change to false
CloudFormation fails; you must manually delete the NAT Gateway first
NAT Gateway is retained if it's in use; deleted if unused
explanation: Conditions control resource creation; changing condition to false removes the resource during update; CloudFormation treats this as resource deletion.

question: You're updating a CloudFormation stack. During the update, the stack enters UPDATE_ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS and gets stuck. You need to resolve this without losing the existing infrastructure. What's the correct action?
options: Use ContinueUpdateRollback API; resume the rollback process to completion
Delete the stack; create a new one with the corrected template
Wait 30 minutes; CloudFormation automatically completes rollback
Edit the template to revert changes; attempt update again
explanation: ContinueUpdateRollback moves stack from stuck state to ROLLBACK_COMPLETE; preserves existing resources; allows retry; deleting the stack is destructive.

question: Your template uses Ref to reference an EC2 instance ID and a Lambda function ARN. Both are created in the same stack. You want to pass these values to an SNS topic's DisplayName. What's the issue?
options: Ref returns physical IDs; instance IDs are valid, but Lambda Ref returns ARN, not function name
Ref can't be used in string interpolation; use Fn::Join instead
Ref is correct; DisplayName accepts any string reference
Ref should be replaced with Fn::GetAtt for better practices
explanation: Ref returns physical IDs (instance-id, function-arn); string interpolation in DisplayName requires Fn::Join or Fn::Sub to concatenate strings with Ref values.

question: You create a CloudFormation stack with an auto-scaling group (ASG). The ASG tags are controlled via CloudFormation's AWS::AutoScaling::LaunchConfiguration. You manually add a new tag via AWS Console. The tag disappears after the stack update. Why?
options: Manual tags are lost during stack updates; CloudFormation overwrites all tags
Tags added outside the template are considered drift; use --no-execute-rollback to preserve them
ASG doesn't support manual tag updates; all tags must be in the template
The tag is retained but hidden; run describe-auto-scaling-groups to verify
explanation: CloudFormation is declarative; template tags replace all tags during updates; manual tags are lost; all tags must be in the template for persistence.

question: You're designing a reusable CloudFormation template for a microservice (Lambda + DynamoDB + API Gateway). The same template needs to deploy 20 independent microservice instances. Should you use StackSets, multiple stacks with parameters, or a single stack with multiple resources?
options: StackSets; deploy to multiple AWS accounts and regions from one template
Multiple stacks with unique names (service-1-stack, service-2-stack); reuse template with different parameters
Single stack with 20 sets of resources; maintains everything in one place
Use a Lambda-backed custom resource to deploy instances programmatically
explanation: Multiple named stacks (one per service) enable independent lifecycle management; StackSets are for multi-account/region; single stack with 20 resources becomes unmanageable; Lambda isn't CloudFormation.
